label: TP
reason: User-supplied header value flows via getHeaders -> nextElement -> URLDecoder.decode -> split(' ')[0] -> doSomething -> bar. The decoded string is then used as input to ESAPI.encodeForHTML which encodes the original bytes, not the HTML-encoded string returned by decode. Since encodeForHTML operates on the raw byte array derived from the decoded string, special characters like '<' remain unescaped in the HTML context, allowing XSS.

evidence.note: Flow from user header to bar variable and subsequent HTML encoding of decoded bytes
